econ-fin-01-c4.text: Ivo Welch (2022). Stock and Bond Valuation: Annuities and Perpetuities (Corporate Finance, ch. 3). Corporate Finance (textbook chapter, corpfin.ivo-welch.org).
econ-fin-01-c4.quote: The growing perpetuity formula allows for a constant rate g per period, provided it is less than the interest rate.
econ-fin-01-c4.claim: A growing perpetuity pays C, then C(1+g), then C(1+g)², forever. Its PV = C/(r-g), provided r > g.

econ-fin-01-c4.text: Ivo Welch (2022). Stock and Bond Valuation: Annuities and Perpetuities (Corporate Finance, ch. 3). Corporate Finance (textbook chapter, corpfin.ivo-welch.org).
econ-fin-01-c4.quote: In this context, the growing perpetuity model is often called the Gordon growth model, after its inventor, Myron Gordon.
econ-fin-01-c4.claim: That's the Gordon growth model, used to price stocks under the assumption of steady dividend growth.

econ-fin-01-c5.text: Campbell R. Harvey and Stephen Gray (1997). Valuation of Cash Flows II: Investment Decisions and Capital Budgeting. Duke University Fuqua School of Business, WWWFinance Global Financial Management.
econ-fin-01-c5.quote: Accept a project if its NPV > 0;
econ-fin-01-c5.claim: The investment decision rule built on present value is short: invest if and only if NPV > 0.
